name: Bizarre Love Polygon
pitch: Pin where and when you fell for someone and watch your love polygon grow on a cute pink map.
facts: Each person you fell for becomes a heart pin on a pink map; the pins form your love polygon.
You can add moments with dates, a place, an emoji and a colour for each person.
Private by design: everything is encrypted on your device, no account, no tracking.
Shows stats such as how many people, countries and how big your polygon is.
Makes Instagram story and post cards of your polygon, with blurred locations and the Polly mascot or your own photo.
Encrypted backup files you can restore on another device.
Works offline and installs as an app on your phone. Also on Google Play for Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.lovepolygon.app
The mascot is Polly, a smiling pink heart-shaped polygon. Polly is just the mascot: Polly never grows or changes. What grows is the user's love polygon, the shape their heart pins make on the map.
screenshot_brief: The image is a phone screenshot of the app showing a pink map with heart pins.
art_hint: For this project, Polly (a smiling pink heart-shaped polygon), heart map pins and pink maps fit well.
card_brief: The image is the app's own share card of a fictional demo user's love polygon. Also invent that demo user's scenario: 3 to 7 fictional people (cute nicknames, never real names) they fell for, each in a real city with its coordinates and dates.

name: 5dollars
pitch: A private ledger for your household's bank accounts: import your statements, categorise them in seconds and see every month whether you saved or spent more than you earned.
facts: No server and no account: 5dollars never sees your data.
Each scenario (for example Personal or Family) is one file that lives where you choose: your Google Drive, a folder on your computer (it can be a synced folder) or this browser.
Share a scenario with your family through Google Drive: Editor can write, Viewer can only read.
Import your bank statements or paste them from Excel or Google Sheets, then categorise moves quickly.
Link the transfers between your own accounts so they don't count as spending.
The report shows, month by month, whether you saved or spent more than you earned, plus your total balance.
Alerts explain months where you saved less than usual, categories running hot and big one-off expenses.
Epics group the moves of a trip, a wedding or a renovation, with their own totals by category, account and month.
An optional public wall page shows only each month's savings and the total balance, for example on a tablet at home.
Data safety: automatic daily and monthly snapshots, and a backup before every delete, restore or merge.
Money is exact, down to the cent.
Made by nubuza.
The mascot is Duro, a smiling gold coin with blush cheeks (in Spain a «duro» was the old 5-peseta coin). Duro is just the mascot, not a feature: the app doesn't talk or give advice.
screenshot_brief: The image is a screenshot of the app with a fictional household: the monthly report chart (did we save each month?), the alerts that explain an unusual month, or a trip epic with its expenses.
art_hint: For this project, Duro (a smiling gold coin with a plum outline and blush cheeks) fits well, with kawaii money around: a smiling piggy bank, a happy little wallet, a cheerful bar chart going up, a cozy home; add 5dollars' green and gold to the nubuza pastels.

name: A Thousand Surnames
pitch: Your ID shows two surnames, but your family tree hides many more. Import your tree or build it by hand and get every surname you carry, in order, with stats and how rare each one is in Spain.
facts: In Spain your 1st surname is your father's 1st and your 2nd is your mother's 1st; your 3rd is your father's 2nd, your 4th your mother's 2nd, and so on: each parent brings their whole list, interleaved with the other's.
Parents give 2 surnames, grandparents 4, great-grandparents 8, great-great-grandparents 16. Ten full generations would give 1,024: about a thousand, hence the name.
Import your family tree from Ancestry, MyHeritage or any program that exports GEDCOM, or build it by hand on a fan chart.
A missing surname shows as "_", and the app gives a clue about which ancestor to research next to fill the first gap.
Stats: generations, how many surnames you know in a row, repeated surnames, and trophies each time you double your surnames in a row (4, 8, 16, 32…).
Rarity uses data from Spain's National Statistics Institute (INE, 1 Jan 2025): how many people in Spain carry each surname and the province where it is most typical.
A just-for-fun counter of how many of your surnames sound Basque (Etxeberria, Goikoetxea, Zubizarreta…). It goes by how a surname looks, not its history.
Two images to share: a kawaii card with all your surnames, and a round fan chart of your family (the "cookie").
Truly private: no accounts and no server. The tree is stored encrypted in your browser and the GEDCOM file is never uploaded. Optional Google Drive sync keeps an encrypted copy only you can open.
Free, in English and Spanish.

The mascot is Kibi, a smiling family cookie: the app's round fan chart baked as a biscuit, with a face in the middle where you are, pastel rings for parents and grandparents, chocolate chips and a bite out of it for the missing ancestors (1,024 is a "kibi" in computing).
Made by nubuza.
card_brief: The image is the app's own share image for a fictional demo person: either the surname card (their first name and every surname in order, with "_" for gaps) or the round family fan chart (the "cookie").
screenshot_brief: The image is a phone screenshot of the app with a fictional family: the numbered surname list with "_" for gaps, the fan-chart family tree, or the stats (generations, surnames in a row, trophies, how many sound Basque).
art_hint: For this project, Kibi (a smiling kawaii cookie, golden-brown crust with chocolate chips and a bite out of the top right, pastel mint, coral, butter, lilac, sky and pink rings around a cream centre with the face), family trees, name tags, old family photos and little houses fit well; add Kibi's mint green, coral red and cookie brown to the nubuza pastels.

name: calview
pitch: Print a blank calendar grid of any size, on one sheet or as a giant wall calendar made of smaller sheets glued together.
facts: A blank calendar grid: 7 columns for the weekdays and one row per week, as many weeks as you like (from a date, or until a date).
Each day has a small number in a tag in the corner of its cell; the first of each month adds the month's initial (1N for November, 1D for December…), so a grid can run across several months.
Any size: A4 to A0, or US Letter, Legal, Tabloid and ANSI C to E, portrait or landscape. Number size, header height, line width and outer border are adjustable.
Collage mode: print a giant calendar (say an A1 for the wall) on ordinary A4 sheets at home, then glue them on top of each other. Nothing is lost under a seam.
Red ticks show where to glue each neighbouring sheet, grey corners show where to trim, and each sheet prints its row and column so the puzzle is easy. An (i) legend explains every mark.
Printer margins are set once for every sheet, with a warning if they are below the recommended minimum.
Settings: English or Spanish, mm or inches, date format, ISO or US paper, and the week can start on Monday, Sunday or Saturday.
Free, no account, no ads: everything runs in the browser and your settings stay on your device.
The mascot is Pip, a smiling yellow pencil with a pink eraser and blushing cheeks, who loves filling empty days with plans. Pip is just the mascot: the calendars come out blank, for you to fill in.
Made by nubuza.
screenshot_brief: The image is a desktop screenshot of the app: the settings panel on the left and the print preview on the right, showing either one blank calendar sheet, a big calendar split across A4 sheets for a collage, or that collage with the legend explaining the glue and trim marks.
art_hint: For this project, Pip (a smiling kawaii yellow pencil with a pink eraser, blush cheeks and a sharpened tip), blank calendar grids, sheets of paper being glued into a big wall calendar, glue sticks, scissors, washi tape and doodled plans fit well; add calview's lavender #b9b0f2 and violet #7c6fd6 to the nubuza pastels.
